questions.q: What is Lightning Web Components built on top of, according to this lesson?
options: A proprietary Salesforce rendering engine with no relationship to standard browser APIs
Native web component browser standards: Custom Elements, Shadow DOM, templates, and ES modules
The same engine that powers Aura components, repackaged under a new name
A server-side rendering framework that sends pre-built HTML pages to the browser
questions.explain: LWC is a thin layer of Salesforce-specific tooling (reactivity, decorators, Salesforce data access) wrapped around native web component standards, which is why LWC code stays close to plain modern JavaScript.

questions.q: Which statement about LWC and Aura coexisting is accurate?
options: An LWC component can contain an Aura component as a child, but not the reverse
Aura has been fully removed from the platform and no longer runs anywhere
An Aura component can contain an LWC component as a child, but an LWC cannot contain an Aura component
LWC and Aura components can never appear on the same Lightning page
questions.explain: Aura components can contain LWC children, but the reverse is not supported — an LWC component cannot contain an Aura component. Both frameworks remain fully supported and commonly coexist in the same org.

questions.q: Which three files are required in every LWC component bundle?
options: A `.css` file, a `.svg` file, and a `__tests__` folder
A `.js` file, a `.html` file, and a `.js-meta.xml` file
A `.json` file, a `.css` file, and a `.js` file
Only a `.html` file — JavaScript and metadata are optional
questions.explain: Every bundle requires a `.js` file (the class), a `.html` file (the template), and a `.js-meta.xml` file (metadata such as API version and exposure). CSS, an SVG icon, and tests are all optional.

questions.q: What is the significance of a component's folder, `.js` file, and `.html` file all sharing the exact same camelCase name?
options: It's purely a style convention with no functional effect
It's how the LWC framework locates the component's related parts — it is a functional requirement, not a style choice
It only matters for components exposed to Lightning App Builder
It is required only when the component contains a test folder
questions.explain: The shared camelCase name across the folder, the `.js` file, and the `.html` file is how the framework connects a component's template, class, and metadata together — this is a functional requirement.

questions.q: Which Salesforce CLI command scaffolds a brand-new Salesforce DX project before any components exist?
options: sf project deploy start
sf lightning generate component --name myComponent
sf project generate --name myProject
sf org login web
questions.explain: `sf project generate` creates the initial Salesforce DX project structure. `sf org login web` authorizes an org, `sf lightning generate component` scaffolds a new bundle inside an existing project, and `sf project deploy start` pushes code to the org.
